text: Mauritanians tend to be direct communicators, especially when talking about things they want. This can seem strange to a visitor, as the phrases “please” and “thank you” are not heard in the course of day to day conversation. It is part of the hospitality of culture. It is the responsibility of the person to provide hospitality to visitors in their home to guests should not have to do anything for themselves. It is only once you become part of the family or a very close friend that Mauritanians will not scold you for getting up and doing something, like getting water for yourself. You can see this in the language as many people will say “Give me the water” or “Hand me the water”. "Please” is never used, but this is not a sign of disrespect. Because it is expected, people will simply demand things, knowing that, when the situation is reversed, they will provide the same hospitality to others in their home.

There is generally very little personal space during conversations. An arm's length is often a good place to start, but often members of the same sex will pull you closer to speak with you. This is a privilege of friends and many will do it in order to convey that they consider you a friend, or want to in any case. People will also do this when asking you for things. There is always space between members of the opposite sex, and usually when you are a guest you will be seated by yourself somewhere, and that amount of space is a rare thing and sort of shows how important they think you are. However, many of the day to day aspects of life in do not allow much space. When traveling in taxis, it's common to see four people placed in the backseat and two in the navigator seat. Drivers try to separate men from women, because things are so squashed, but this does not always work, and foreigners are often used as buffers between Mauritanian men and women. Members of the opposite sex do not touch, in general. Although some men may shake the hands of foreign women if they are presented in a business context, this varies on the area. Moors from the north seldom if ever touch women, but Pulaar and Woloof men in the south are generally less conservative. There is a considerable amount of touching between members of the same sex while conversing. Holding hands is common, and does not indicate anything other than friendship.

Many children will not look their elders in the eye, women may not look a man in the eye, but this is not always the case, and women in Mauritanian culture generally have more freedom and status than is seen in other Arab cultures. When speaking to a high ranking religious official, such as an imam or a maribou, people will generally not look them in the eye. Visiting Westerners tend to come with a strange kind of status, and looking people in the eye in not something most Mauritanians will take offense to.

While in general it is best to be on time, it is rare for meetings to start on time, if they start at all. People who come late are generally unabashed, and will not see their tardiness as any reason not to stop and greet everyone before sitting down to the meeting. Regarding transportation, Mauritania has few train or bus services. The train that runs from Zourat to Nouadibou is run by a private company, and is generally on time. When getting into a taxi, the driver will always tell you they are leaving immediately, or in five minutes. Taxis will leave when they have acquired enough passengers to fill the car, which can take anywhere from 5 minutes to an hour or more. The bac, the barge between Rosso and Rosso , generally runs on time. No matter how far behind or how much work there is to be done, everything stops for at least an hour in the afternoon for lunch and a rest. This can take up to 3 hours. The idea of taking a quick break and heading back to work does not tend to apply in Mauritania. There usually must be a meal and at least 2 of the 3 rounds of tea before you can start work again. Few people work between 1 pm and 3:30 pm. Also, everything stops for prayer times as well. Most people give their time to others freely.

While women in Mauritanian society can be found running boutiques by themselves, selling at their own stalls in the market place, and serving in positions within the government, they must conform to a different set of behavioral standards. Women seldom travel alone between cities, and if they do a male relative generally escorts them to the garage and arranges their fare and car with the samsaar (the head of the garage) himself. Women cover their head, either by wearing a mulafa, a full body veil a little like a sari which covers the head but not the face (although the free end may be used to wrap around the face during sandstorms or if a woman is in the presence of many men and feels the need to cover her face), or by wearing a head wrap, typical of the Woloof, Sonnika, and Pulaar women, a colorful piece of fabric that matches the rest of their outfit. When in the company of women, moors may let the head cover part of their mulafa fall back, but they always adjust it before leaving the home. Foreign women are not expected to cover their heads, but those that choose to wear tank tops that reveal their shoulders, tight clothes, pants, and skirts that are not full length risk being dubbed “disquette”. In some circumstances this means “pretty young girl” but it is not a word men will use to describe a respected Mauritanian woman. Women traveling will be better respected if they wear clothes that cover their shoulders, knees, and ankles. If pants are worn, the shirt should be longer, falling halfway to the knees. Headcovering is not mandatory, but may be a good idea when meeting higher level officials, as they will respond positively to the gesture.

People beckon one another by holding the palm out and opening and closing the fingers. It usually means “come here”. Snapping your fingers over your shoulder means you are talking about something that happened a long time ago. Some drivers will demand your “pass” by rubbing their thumb over their index and pointer fingers. When discussing two people who are a couple, people will hook their two pointer fingers together, first with one finger on top, and then again with the opposite finger on top. Strangers will often try to get your attention by saying “Psssst.” Over, and over, and over. Placing your thumb under your chin means “a lot.”

Lying on the back is usually not acceptable for women and lying on the stomach is not acceptable for men. No displays of public affection between members of the opposite sex are accepted. Married couples are not allowed to hold hands, and it is often difficult to identify husbands and wives because they seldom sit together and never touch. Ignoring people who greet you is considered extremely rude. When one enters a store or house or any public place it is necessary to greet people you see. During the holy month of Ramadan, drinking or eating in front of Mauritanians is particularly rude. It is seen as shameful for a boy and girl to flirt together in public. Within the Maure ethnicity, it is seen negatively if a woman raises her head covering in public.

Mauritania is a dry country and d rinking is illegal under sharia law. Foreigners can sometimes find beer in various restaurants in the capital and can consume it legally, but bringing alcohol into the country and giving any to Mauritanians is illegal. Once every few months there will be a crackdown on the restaurants and clubs that sell beer, and there will not be any to be found for a while before things loosen up again. If there are smoking laws they are not enforced, although smoking is not allowed for Mauritanians during Ramadan, and discouraged for women. Penalties for possession, use, or trafficking in illegal drugs in are severe, and convicted offenders can expect long jail sentences and heavy fines.

There are many restaurants in the capital which are run by foreigners that will happily serve meals between sunrise and sunset during Ramadan. If working in rural areas, remember that the rainy season can effectively delay a project for weeks or months, since with few paved roads the water can limit transportation to and from the city for days after the rain. Foreigners will always be charged more, and the price is hardly ever listed for anything, so it is a good idea to get the typical prices from someone you trust before negotiating, which is necessary for most things you buy in the market, and all transportation. Items you buy in a small boutique, like washing powder, sugar, rice, cookies, milk, etc. usually have fixed prices, and owner will not negotiate. Observe what the Mauritanian customers are doing first if you are unsure. Garages/taxi stands can be stressful as once you arrive your will most likely immediately be surrounded by a large group of men, all telling you to come with them. They will grab your bags form the trunk if you are not fast enough and carry them to their vehicle. It is the one place in where strangers, men, will touch a woman. They know this is inappropriate, and they do it because you are a westerner, do remind then sharply and loudly that they should not be touching you and they will back off. Stand your ground and demand the prices before you get into a car. There are several classes of vehicle. Almost all the cars are Mercedes or Peugot station wagons. A Mercedes will hold fewer and go faster, a Peugot is cheaper, but holds more people (3 in the back, 4 in the middle, two in the front plus the driver) so it takes longer to fill. You may find a car that will only carry a “normal” western load, of 3 in the back and 1 in the front, these generally cater to richer customers, and you will pay more, but have a more comfortable ride. Also keep in mind that most Mauritanian women are large, fat is considered beautiful, so you will be more comfortable sharing a backseat with 3 skinny men than 3 large women. Your bags will cost extra, but you can negotiate this down, they should not cost extra between Rosso and Nouakchott , because it is a short ride. Cars also frequently break down, so be prepared to stop for a flat tire, and try to pick a car that looks in better condition than the rest. Getting together a group of 6 before arriving at the garage saves time, as you can rent out the entire car and leave immediately. When traveling north from Rosso there are 5-7 checkpoints, some run by the police and some by the army, and the driver will have to get out and usually pay a bribe. You will also be asked for your passports as well. This is less common on roads that do not lead to or from a border, such as the Road of Hope that heads east, or the road north to Atar. Be prepared to drink a lot of sugar mint tea.

While in general it is best to be on time for meetings, it is rare for them to start on time, if they start at all. People who come late are generally unabashed, and will not see their tardiness as any reason not to stop and greet everyone before sitting down to the meeting.

Foreigners will almost always be charged more for goods and services. Prices are rarely listed so it is a good idea to get the typical prices from someone you trust before negotiating, which is necessary for most things you buy in the market, and all transportation. Items bought in a small boutique, like washing powder, sugar, rice, cookies, milk, etc. usually have fixed prices, and the owners do not tend to negotiate. Observe what the Mauritanian customers are doing first if you are unsure.

The grading system at most institutions is based on the French system of 0-20, with 20 being the highest. A 20 is next-to-impossible to earn though, 11s and 12s are average. Below 10 is failing. Lecture is the most common form of teaching.
Dating is very undercover and secretive, especially within the family. Arranged marriage is still practiced.

독립(19 2차 세계대전 이후 AOF 내에선 동 시기 다른 식민지들과 마찬가지로 민족주의 열풍과 함께 독립 요구가 거세짐. 살렉 쿠데타부터 타야 쿠데타까지(1978~19 1978년 쿠데타로 정권을 잡은 무스타파 울드 살렉은 국가회복군사 위원회( )를 만들고 CMRN : Comité Militaire de Redressement National 20명의 위원을 임명하며 군부 통치를 시작함. 취임 이후 엘 가즈아니 대통령은 부패 근절, 빈곤 및 사회적 불평등 해결을 기조로 정책을 추진하였으며, 울드 압델 아지즈 전(前) 대통령의 부패 혐의에 대해서도 적극적으로 수사하는 등 이전 정권과의 차별성을 강조함. 취임 이후 엘 가즈아니 대통령은 부패 근절, 빈곤 및 사회적 불평등 해결을 기조로 정책을 추진하였으며, 울드 압델 아지즈 전(前) 대통령의 부패 혐의에 대해서도 적극적으로 수사함으로써 전 정권과의 차별성을 부각시킴.

또한 중국은 도로 철도 항만 발전소 등 모리타니아의 인프라 부문에 막대한 투자를 시행 중 - 누 악쇼트-나즐렛 카이레 고속도로(Nouakchott-Nazlet Khayre Highway), 누아디부 항구(Nouadhibou Port) 확장, 누악쇼트 국제공항 확장 등 인프라 프로젝트에 투자 중 중 국은 모리타니아의 광업 분야, 특히 철광석 채굴 분야의 최대 투자국 중 하나 ▲ 농수산업, ▲문화 및 교육 분야에서도 협력을 강화 중이며, 중국은 누악쇼트와 누아디부에 공자학원을 설립하여 중국어와 중국 문화를 전파하는 한편, 모리타니아 학생들의 중국 유학을 위해 장학금을 제공하고 있음.

모리타니아-걸프협력회의(GCC) 국가들과의 관계 모리타니아는 동일한 이슬람의 가치 및 아랍 민족사에 역사적 뿌리를 두고 있는 걸프협력회의 국가들과 우호적 협력적 관계를 유지 중 - 특 히 GCC 국가들은 광업 에너지 인프라 부문에서 모리타니아의 주요 투자국이고, 모리타니아에 상당한 개발 원조를 제공하여 교육 의료 농업 등의 분야에서 다양한 프로젝트를 지원 - 양 측은 리비아 분쟁과 시리아 위기 등에 대한 입장을 조율해 왔고, 모리타니아는 GCC 전력망사업당국(GCCIA : GCC Interconnection Authority)과 같이 GCC가 주도하는 이니셔티브에 적극 참여 마.

아프리카와의 관계 모리타니아는 다른 아프리카 국가들과 강력하고 다각적인 관계를 유지하며, 지역 협력, 경제 협력 및 문화 교류를 지속 중 모 리타니아는 아프리카연합(AU), 서아프리카경제공동체(ECOWAS), 아랍마그레브연합(UMA)에 참여 중이며, 아프리카 국가들과의 양자 무역협정 및 아프리카대륙자유무역지대(AfCFTA) 체결 아프리카 국가와의 관계 사례 세네갈 : 모리타니아의 가장 가까운 이웃 국가로, 양국은 오랜 협력의 역사를 공유하면서, 국경 보안, 인프라 개발 및 무역 촉진에 대해 협력하고 있음. 말 리 : 모리타니아와 말리는 문화적 유대감이 강하며 대테러, 지역 안정 및 경제 개발과 같은 문제에 대해 협력하고 있음. 다만 말리에서의 연이은 쿠데타 발생에 따라 양국 협력이 제한되는 상황임. 모 로코 : 모리타니아와 모로코는 최근 몇 년 동안 무역, 투자, 문화 교류에 중점을 두고 관계를 강화해 왔음.

- 모 리타니아 정부는 농촌 지역 전기 공급 및 세네갈강 계곡 농업 기계화 지원 등 농업 생산량 확대를 통해 수입 의존도를 낮추고 식량 안보를 확보하고자 노력 중 목축업은 GDP의 약 9.8%를 차지하며 모리타니아의 식량안보 및 지역 경제에 기여하는 주요 산업 부문이나, 전통 유목 방식에다 소규모로 이루어지기 때문에 강우량 등 기후 조건에 따라 변동성이 커서 종합적 관리와 성장에 한계가 있음.

53 경 제 - 다 만 대부분 전통적인 소규모 어업 방식을 택하고 있고, 어획량의 상당 부분이 모리타니아에서 하역되거나 가공되지 않고 유럽(스페인 등)과 일본으로 직접 수출되고 있으며, 튀르키예와 중국 기업들이 중국으로 수출하기 위해 어분(魚粉)으로 전환하는 어획량도 증가 수산업은 직접 종사자 6만 5천 명, 간접 종사자 약 20만 명으로 모리타니아 내 주요 고용 부문인 만큼, 모리타니아 정부는 동 부문의 개혁, 연구조사, 어족 자원 모니터링 및 관리 등에 중점을 두고 정책을 추진 중이며, 2020~2024 수산 전략에 따라 모리타니아 기업과 외국인 투자자 간의 합작투자를 촉진하여 국내 어류 가공 및 부가가치 창출을 늘리는 것을 목표로 하고 있음.

통 계 출산율은 4.4명, 기대수명은 65세 (2021년, 출처 : World Bank) 인구의 42%가 14세 이하이고, 65세 이상 인구가 3%에 불과한, 매우 젊은 나라 (2022년, World Bank 통계) 단, 국토의 약 80%에 이르는 광활한 사막 영토로 인해 인구밀도는 km2당 4명에 불과하여 인구밀도가 가장 낮은 나라 중 하나 63 사회 문화 2 언 어 공식 언어는 아랍어로, 모리타니아의 아랍어 방언은 하사니아 (Hasaniya)라고 불림. 역사적으로 싱게티(Chinguetti) 등 오아시스를 중심으로 형성된 도시 들은 사하라를 가로질러 이슬람교와 문화를 전파하는 중요한 역할을 하였음. 전통 의상 모리타니아의 전통 의상은 사막의 모래바람과 뜨거운 태양으로부터 착용자를 보호하는 기능을 하며, 시내에서도 전통 의상을 입은 사람들을 흔히 볼 수 있음. 모리타니아 남성들의 다라(Daraa) 의상 모리타니아 여성들의 물라파(Mulafa) 의상 65 사회 문화 나.

전통 가옥 11~12세기부터 사하라 사막을 건너는 카라반 상인들의 중간 휴식을 위해 돌과 진흙으로 만든 크사르(Ksour)로 불리는 전통 가옥이 지어짐. 문화적 특징 모리타니아의 문화는 유목민의 특성, 아랍-이슬람 양식을 기본으로 하며, 이외에도 프랑스・아프리카 토속 문화도 혼재되어 있음. 테이딘(T’heydinn)과 그리오(griot) 모리타니아는 시를 짓고 낭송하는 문화가 발달하여 아랍권에서 ‘천 명의 시인의 땅(The Land of a Thousand Poets)’이라 불리기도 함. 테이딘은 무어인들의 역사와 문화를 담은 서사시로, 그리오라는 세습 음유시인들이 티드니트(Tidnit), 아르딘(Ardin) 등 전통 현악기, 팀파니 반주와 함께 노래하는 종합예술임. 그리오들의 노령화와 숫자 감소로, 테이딘 역시 존속에 위협을 받고 있어 2011년 유네스코 무형문화유산 긴급보호목록에 등재됨.

유네스코 무형문화유산 ▲대추야자와 관련된 지식과 기술, 전통과 관습(20, ▲쿠스쿠스의 생산 및 소비와 관련된 지식, 노하우와 관습(20, ▲아랍어 캘리 그래피 : 지식, 기술 및 관행(20 문화가 다른 아랍 국가들과 공동 으로 유네스코 무형문화유산 목록에 등재되었음. 모스크를 중심으로 구성된 마을과 성벽이 사하라 지역 유목 민족의 전통적인 주거 형태를 잘 보여주고 있음. 71 사회 문화 우아단 고대 도시 방다르갱 국립공원(Banc d’Arguin National Park) : 모리타니아 북서쪽에 위치한 국립공원으로, 모래언덕, 해안 습지, 섬 등으로 이루어져 있어 다양한 생물종이 서식하고 있으며, 철새들의 겨울 서식지이기도 함. 사하라의 눈 73 사회 문화 쿰비살레(Koumbi Saleh) : 모리타니아 남동부에 위치한 중세 유적지로 가나 제국(9~13세기)의 수도였으며, 1900년대에 발견되어 발굴 작업이 진행 중 쿰비살레 VIIIII 한-모리정타 니치아 관계 1.

상주 공관을 철수하고 주모로코 대한민국 대사관에서 모리타니아를 겸임 - 모리타니아는 주일본 모리타니아 대사관에서 우리나라를 겸임 중 우리나라와 모리타니아는 지리적 거리가 매우 멀고, 문화 종교적으로 이질적이며 양국 국민 간 교류 역사가 깊지 않음에도 불구하고, 양국 정부는 1963년 수교 이래 정치・경제・문화 등 제반 분야에서 우호 협력 관계를 유지해 왔음. 양국 간 협정 체결 현황 어업협정 (1984.1월) 문화협정 (1989.6월) 무역협정 (1989.7월) 투자보장협정 (2006.7월) 라.
